To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the in-medium modifications of the meson spectral function are small in small collision systems.
the in-medium modifications of the spectral functions are tiny for small systems.

the time evolution of vector meson spectral functions in the BUU model is driven by the in-medium density and that in-medium modifications of vector meson propagators are tiny for small systems like C + C at the HADES energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How does the time evolution of the vector meson spectral functions look like? What is the influence on the di-electron production? How can we interpret the experimental data?
the propagation of vector mesons in a hot and dense medium.
the propagation of spectral functions in the framework of a BUU type model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HADES data are not compatible with the assumption of in-medium modified vector mesons.

the di-electron data from the HADES Collaboration can neither be interpreted as evidence for the formation of a hot and dense phase in the collision system, nor can they be used to draw conclusions about the in-medium properties of vector mesons.
the HADES data can be described by a model which does not include in-medium modifications of the vector mesons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the di-electron mass-spectrum is dominated by the direct decay of mesons, whereas the contribution of in-medium modified mesons is small.
the di-electron data are not yet sufficient to constrain the vector-meson spectral-function.
a transport approach is not able to reproduce the observed in-medium modifications of the vector meson spectral-functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the di-electron mass spectrum in small collision systems is dominated by the initial conditions.
the in-medium modifications of the vector-mesons are very sensitive to the choice of the in-medium spectral functions.
the spectral function is a useful concept in the context of transport models.
